title: Window-starvation event: adaptive circuit breaker, tenant fairness tokens, and observability improvements
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2026-02-18 we observed repeated 'batch lull' episodes on prod-serving clusters in eu-west-1 where the continuous batcher would stop forming batches for up to 1.2s despite steady incoming traffic. Symptoms included sudden tail-Q95/Q99 spikes for small-token requests, tenant-visible request pinning, and reduced throughput on affected GPUs. Investigations showed a confluence of factors: (1) adaptive KV-cache prefetching increased lock hold time under particular sequence-length distributions, (2) a timing regression in the coalescer's timer backoff caused exponential growth of per-slot wait windows for threads that had just missed a deadline, and (3) a tenant with many low-latency short requests monopolized batch-formation slots due to lack of per-tenant admission safeguards.

Root cause: The primary trigger was the coalescer timer backoff regression (introduced in runtime-1.18) that multiplied the nominal batching window for certain wakeups. In isolation that only increases batching latency slightly; however, when combined with longer KV-cache lock sections during prefix retrieval and a skewed client mix (heavy small-token traffic from a single tenant), the scheduler experienced priority inversion where starving streams waited multiple backoff periods and never coalesced into healthy batches. This produced a feedback loop: starving requests delayed batch completion, which lengthened queueing for other tenants and amplified the tail.

Impact: Intermittent Q95/Q99 tail latency spikes for text generation and chat endpoints in eu-west-1 over two 40-minute incident windows. Several mid-market customers reported degraded interactive responsiveness (customer support tickets referenced). No data loss or model-state corruption.

Mitigations already applied: (a) Emergency rollback of the coalescer timer change to previous stable behavior (runtime-1.19 rollback) on 2026-02-18 21:12 UTC; (b) short-term per-tenant concurrency cap applied for tenants with >1000 RPS of sub-50-token requests; (c) increased alert sensitivity for batch-formation stalls (new alert rule and playbook link below).

Decisions and trade-offs: We prioritize restoring interactivity and fairness over absolute throughput in the short term. The adaptive circuit-breaker design proposed below intentionally trades a small amount of throughput to bound tail latency and avoid tenant monopolization. Long-term kernel-level optimizations to KV-cache locking are desirable but higher risk and will be staged.
action_items: A1: Implement 'batch-lull detector' in the coalescer that enforces a hard upper bound (configurable) on per-slot wait time and emits a diagnostic span when hit. Owner: Miguel. Due: 2026-03-05.

A2: Build an adaptive circuit-breaker that, when batch-formation stalls are detected, temporarily reduces windows for noisy tenants and grants token credits to starving request classes to re-balance fairness. Owner: Priya Menon. Estimate: 5 pts. Target release: runtime-1.20.

A3: Introduce per-tenant small-request token bucket (soft policing) to prevent single-tenant slot domination; default thresholds and opt-in for high-tier customers. Owner: Platform team (Kai). Due: 2026-03-12.

A4: Reduce lock granularity in KV-cache path: split prefix retrieval into read-mostly fast path and write path with a micro-lock. Spike PR by 2026-03-01; full rollout in runtime-1.21. Owner: Cache team (Liu Wei).

A5: Add observability: chart 'batch_wait_distribution' by tenant and model; add trace-level tag when lull detector triggers; surface in Console alerting and per-route latency breakdown dashboards. Owner: Observability (Hannah). Due: 2026-03-08.
A6: Create a canary plan to push circuit-breaker to dedicated pools first and monitor tail latency with synthetic short-token workloads before host-wide rollout. Owner: SRE (Ethan). Due: 2026-03-10.
A7: Run a 72-hour post-fix soak in eu-west-1 with increased synthetic coverage for mixed-length workloads and report findings to execs. Owner: Reliability (Asha). Due: 2026-03-20.

notes: Avoid heavy-handed global knobs in the medium term; prefer targeted tenant-level controls and observable signals so we can iterate without impacting overall cluster throughput.
This incident highlights subtle interactions between coalescer timing heuristics and cache lock latency; add this as a recurring discrepancy test in our CI performance harness.
Follow-up retro scheduled 2026-03-07 15:00 UTC; attendees: runtime, cache, SRE, observability, platform, product-owner. Agenda: A1-A7 review and canary checklist.
